_note: Body expression (pepin.expression): the gesture engine and the speaker gaze, run inside the voice cascade on the laptop. The atoms, compositions, taught poses and idle layers are config/animation.json; the arm's caps, limits and rest pose, which the board enforces, are config/arm.json's motion block; the face finder's detector is config/face_sensor.json's. Every number here is a design default until a line says MEASURED.

flags.note: The two features' switches at the cascade's start; while it runs: scripts/voice_cascade.py switch --flag gestures=on (data/voice/control.json's flags, answered in control.jsonl). Switching a feature on re-reads this file and config/animation.json. gestures: every gesture and idle layer of every part (arm, head overlays, face cues, wheels); off, markers are still taken out of the speech and nothing moves. speaker_gaze: the head's base layer on the person and its turn of the wheels.

timing.note: audio_lag_s: how much later the speaker sounds than the player's clock says a block plays (the board's aplay start, config/face.json's lipsync start_latency_s 0.12, unmeasured, plus the WiFi hop): a cue fires this much later. char_s: seconds per spoken character while a part's audio is still being made (Player.heard's estimate). late_s: a clip whose time has passed by at most this is sent at once, a later one is dropped and logged (a stroke shifted 0.5 s still looks natural on a word; the first part of a reply plays as soon as it is made, so its preparations are late by their length). poll_s: how often the engine looks at the player's clock while a clip waits for its word.

layers.note: fade_s: per part, how long a layer change eases (the face in 0.1 s, the body in 0.35 s: Disney's bipedal character); the arm's is the board's own way to rest at its caps. The person starting to speak fades the gesture layer of every part, even while the robot is silent, but a gesture of finish (a greeting, a farewell) already past its stroke and ending within finish_s plays out. idle_resume_s: quiet on a part after a gesture before its idle layer plays again; idle_after_speech_s: no idle motion this soon after anyone spoke. face_hold_s: how long a {face:NAME} marker's expression holds. seed: null draws a fresh seed for each performance (logged with it); a number makes every performance repeat (the bench).

caps.note: What the brain's markers and the robot's moments may play (a tool or scripts/gesture.py, which a person asked for, is never capped); a marker over a cap is dropped and logged. per_part: gestures in one voice part (a sentence, or a clause a style cut); per_reply, per_minute: of all gestures; arm_per_minute: gestures with the arm (over it the rest of the gesture plays without the arm); intent_per_minute: an intent's own; a composition's cooldown_s (config/animation.json) between two of its own. The person's laugh (laughter, a regex on what Whisper read, within laughter_s) waives the caps of laughter_waives. From expressive_motion.md: a person telling a story makes ~4 gestures a minute; no study gives an annoyance threshold: these are starting knobs.

arm.note: latency_s: the WiFi hop and the board's next tick. speed_scale: every arm clip's time stretched by 1/speed_scale and the servos' profile capped by it; 0.2 for the first live test, raised by Artem's word. knot_hz: the knots a clip is sampled into (the board interpolates between them on its 50 Hz tick).

head.note: latency_s: the door's HTTP, the arbiter's step and the neck_target hop.

face.note: latency_s: the head server's hop; its 280 ms tween (config/face.json timing) starts after it.

finder.note: Where the speaker gaze's face detector (SCRFD, det_10g) runs: compute_units is CoreML's CPUAndNeuralEngine (the CPU and the Neural Engine, never the GPU, where the voice's Qwen3-TTS runs: on 2026-10-12 the voice's first chunk took 230-400 ms with the detector free to use the GPU against 100-150 ms without the gaze), ALL (CoreML chooses, the GPU included: as before), CPUAndGPU, or CPU (onnxruntime's own CPU provider); a network CoreML refuses runs on the CPU, said once in the log. bodies: the people detector beside the face detector, vision (Apple Vision's VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest, on the Neural Engine: 3.0 ms median at 800x600, +110-125 MB, MEASURED 2026-10-12 with scratch/gaze/vision_probe.swift; needs pyobjc-framework-Vision: uv add --group macos pyobjc-framework-Vision, without it the finder says so once and runs faces only) or none. body_head_frac: an upright person's head is this share of their box's height below its top (a lying person's box: its middle; a box the frame's top edge cuts: that edge).

wheels.note: The wheels' expressive motions (pepin.expression.wheels: the speaker gaze's turn toward a person past the forward arc (speaker.arc_deg), the gestures' body atoms): twist lines from this Mac to the board's base server over its own link (the measured motions' method, never Nav2), judged by the base server's wheel odometry; nothing new runs on the board. Read again at every motion (the gesture engine reads speed_scale when gestures switch on: it stretches the body's clips). max_turn_deg: the most one request turns (more is refused, never clamped); step_deg: a turn tells its progress every step_deg (the speaker gaze reads the odometry's heading itself ten times a second while a turn runs); max_rock_m: the most a rock or a body clip drives. attempts, backoff_m, max_backoff_m: a turn that stalls or whose arc is blocked backs off backoff_m (its rear checked) and turns the rest again, at most attempts tries and max_backoff_m of backing in all, then gives up (the head looks as far as it reaches); a halt, someone else's command, a drive or a refused check never retries. speed_scale: every cap below times it (ramps times its square, as a clip stretched by 1/speed_scale moves); 0.4 (2026-10-12, Artem: the turn toward a call from behind was too slow at 0.2), raised by Artem's word. yaw_rate_deg_s, yaw_acc_deg_s2: the turn's top rate and ramp at speed 1 (30 deg/s swings the rear corners, 0.41 m out, at 0.21 m/s; a wheel rim at 0.14 m/s of config/base.json's 0.30); the ramp 360 makes the turn decisive rather than cautious: at speed 0.4 the rate is 12 deg/s, reached in 0.21 s at 57.6 deg/s^2 (1.0 rad/s^2, the ramp Nav2's rotate-to-heading uses on this cart, ros/params/nav2_params.yaml max_angular_accel), so a 30 deg turn's profile is 2.7 s (6.7 s at 0.2 and 90; on the simulated base 2.5 s against 5.3: scratch/gaze/turn_time.py), plus 0.1-0.6 s of checks before the first twist; at a speed_scale over 0.56 the ramp passes the velocity smoother's 2.0 rad/s^2 (lower it with the scale); speed_m_s, acc_m_s2: a straight leg's (the rock, the back-off). DESIGN DEFAULTS, UNMEASURED: what the servos follow over the WiFi is the first live test's question. settle_deg, settle_m: a leg this close to its target (or past it) is done. clearance_m: the swept footprint (config/base.json) must keep this far from every lidar return it moves toward (the goal server's newest scan; returns below the lidar's plane, 0.38 m, are not seen); 0.5 means nobody within half a metre of the swept cart. lidar_age_s: an older scan is no scan (refused). stall_s: a leg that makes less than a third of its commanded motion over this long is stalled. stop_hold_s: after someone else's stop during a motion (the red button, the teleop's stop) every motion is refused this long. latency_s: from a gesture's cue to the first motion (the goal server's first answer, the WiFi).

doa.measured: MEASURED 2026-10-12 (ros/tools/doa_calibrate.py): front 170, left 106, behind 343, right 278 deg; quarter-turn misses +0, -26, +7, -18
doa.note: The XVF3800 sits on the cart's front-left (where the left arm would be), not on the head. readings: the array's angle (0..359, 0 toward its USB-C side) of a voice 1.5 m in front of, left of, behind and right of the cart; the bearing is interpolated between them (front, left, behind, right are 0, +90, 180, -90 deg exactly), which absorbs the off-centre array's uneven quarters. front_deg and sign (+1 when the angle grows toward the cart's left, -1 toward its right) alone turn the angle by an offset when the four are not all known. ros/tools/doa_calibrate.py --write measures and writes all of it (one phrase three times at each place; it refuses a reading nearer another quarter than its own); front_deg and sign null and no readings: the gaze orients by faces alone (the head tilts to seek_tilt_deg where it points and looks for a face). window_s: the speech-flagged readings of the utterance's last window_s (the utterance's end mapped onto the board's clock by the newest reading) are averaged (circular mean) into its bearing; fewer than min_speech of them (about 10 a second arrive) and the voice has no bearing.

speaker.note: The speaker gaze is one engine (pepin.expression.tracker): stimuli (the array's DOA stream with the robot's own speaking spans cut out, utterances, one head-camera frame of faces and people's boxes) place a few PEOPLE TRACKS (pepin.expression.tracks), the POLICY engages the person speaking (pepin.expression.policy) and the head moves in one eased aim, pan and tilt together. MOTION: turn_speed_deg_s, turn_acc_deg_s2, adjust_acc_deg_s2: every aim is an angles look with the servo's own trapezoid as its ease (neck_target's speed_deg_s and acc_deg_s2): a TURN to a new person at turn_acc_deg_s2 (650: 20 deg in 0.35 s, 60 deg in 0.61 s, peaks 114 and 198 deg/s, a human head's coarse turn), an ADJUSTMENT (onto the face, a person moving, the voice followed, the seek's stops, the body's turn re-centred) at adjust_acc_deg_s2 (400: 6 deg in 0.25 s, 20 deg in 0.45 s, 40 deg in 0.63 s); both capped at turn_speed_deg_s; the board keeps the tilt's own 600 deg/s^2 ramp under them, so a combined move arcs; 0 for a ramp: the arbiter's saccade or slow speed instead (as before 2026-10-12). THE BODY, one rule: arc_deg (160, 0..360: +-80 deg of the cart's nose, Artem 2026-10-12): the head alone serves any bearing within this forward arc; the person engaged past it turns the body toward them (to face them, at most wheels.max_turn_deg a request, asked again while they are still past it: 150 deg is 30, 30, 30), the wheels started before the head's aim and neither waiting for the other (the head, the fast one, arrives first); not during a check, and while the wheels cannot (a refused check, a stall, a blocked arc, the caps) the head alone stays on the person as far as it reaches: a refusal or a cut turn is asked again at the person's next utterance, a turn that moved the cart and still fell short not again for that person in the conversation (no creeping back-offs). The person speaking never stops it (it is the base layer, as the head's tracking is; the gestures' motions do stop). THE FRAME: the people's bearings are kept in the cart's frame at the newest heading of the wheels' odometry (the base server's state lines, on the board's clock, whoever turned the cart): a turn since is taken off every person, off each of the array's readings by its own stamp (an utterance spoken across a turn gives the bearing the person has now; gaze_doa rows then carry the degrees taken off), and the head re-centres on the person as the body comes round under it (a seek's stop keeps its place in the room). PEOPLE: a face gives a person's head aim; a body box (finder.bodies) an estimate of it (finder.body_head_frac), so a standing, sitting or lying person is aimed at without a face; a voice gives a bearing at the track's remembered tilt, seek_tilt_deg for a new one (+3: the faces seen on 2026-10-12 sat at +0.6..+6.3 deg, median +3.2; the picture is 59 deg tall, so a standing face at 1 m, -19 deg, is in it too). match_deg: a face or a body this near a person's bearing is that person; voice_match_deg: a voice this near is theirs (the array read 5-14 deg off the face at a normal level), else a new voice-only person. tilt_hysteresis_deg (12, 0..30): the person's tilt changes its source, a face's to a body box's estimate or back, only when the two differ by more than this (the pan follows the newest sighting either way; one source moves its own tilt freely); the head nodded between Artem's face and his box on 2026-10-12 (one switch logged stepped the tilt 10.5 deg: scratch/gaze/tilt_sources.py); a posture change (sitting down, standing up: 15-30 deg at 1-2 m) still moves it. DESIGN DEFAULT. seen_fresh_s: a person seen (face or body) this recently keeps their place against the voice; an older one takes the fresh voice's bearing and keeps its tilt (a stale place never wins over a fresh bearing). max_tracks, track_forget_s: people kept, and forgotten when unseen and unheard this long (kept across conversations for their tilt; a drive forgets them). WHOM: the robot's name always turns the head (a seek, no return); words from a person seen before switch at once; words from a voice with nobody seen there while someone seen is engaged make a check: one frame within verify_s there, back when nobody; with nobody engaged a seek. doa_min_speech, doa_min_dbfs: an utterance without words, with fewer speech-flagged readings, or a peak under doa_min_dbfs never moves the head, the name aside (2026-10-12: at -16 dBFS or louder the bearing was 5-14 deg off the face, n 8; at -20..-22 dBFS 28, 72 and 76 deg off in three of four, at -30 76 deg: scratch/gaze/doa_vs_face.py). An utterance overlapping the robot's speech keeps its clean readings (outside the robot's spans and 0.3 s after); fewer than doa_min_speech of them: it moves nothing. SEEK (the person engaged has a bearing, nobody is seen there): seek_frames frames seek_every_s apart at each place, first the voice of the last doa_follow_s (moved more than doa_moved_deg: go there), then seek_pan_deg outward of the bearing and as far inward at the same tilt (outward first: the three misses logged had the face further from the nose than the voice), then back to the voice; a person within seek_pan_deg + match_deg of the bearing is the one sought; no tilt sweep. FOLLOW: while the person speaks and nobody has seen them for seen_fresh_s the head follows the voice's clean speech readings of the last doa_follow_s (at least follow_min_speech of them), in steps over doa_moved_deg and at most follow_max_deg (a jump is a new voice, judged when its utterance ends). seek_min_face_px, track_min_face_px: faces from seek_min_face_px wide count near a person known and while seeking (a 0.15 m face is ~40 px at 2 m, ~26 px at 3 m; config/face_sensor.json); a new person needs track_min_face_px; a face under it is aimed at but not smiled at. min_body_score: a body box scored under it is nobody (Vision scored the people of 2026-10-05's frames 0.55-0.76). track_hz: frames a second while the robot listens and the head stands still, is the speaker's and carries no gesture (a breath does not count): a 42 KB snapshot (~45 ms of network wait), SCRFD on the Neural Engine (5.6 ms) and the body detector (3 ms), on the gaze's own thread; at the arbiter's door a still person costs 600 state reads and 30 renewals a minute and no aim. track_speaking_hz: the rate while the robot speaks (its voice uses the GPU). hold_for_voice: from a reply's first part going to the voice until its first chunk is with the player, no frame and no detection (2026-10-12: the first chunk took 230-400 ms with the gaze on, 100-150 without). lead_s, lead_max_deg: a moving person is aimed where they will be lead_s later (their speed over the last two sightings, pan only), at most lead_max_deg ahead. refine_deg: after a turn, a person further than this off the frame's centre is centred. deadband_deg: while tracking, a person this close to the centre moves nothing. saccade_over_deg: a correction larger than this is a turn, a smaller one an adjustment. aim_min_deg: an aim less than this from the last one is not written. face_lost_s, face_lost_frames: the person engaged is lost after face_lost_frames frames without them AND face_lost_s (at the 1 Hz of the robot's speech one missed frame is no loss); the head then goes to their voice when it was heard while nothing saw them, else stays; frames go on. ttl_s, renew_s: the speaker's look lives ttl_s and is renewed every renew_s, so the head goes home within ttl_s of the cascade's end; a renewal that finds the look gone (a look the person asked for took the head) asks again, queued behind it. aim_wait_s: how long an aim waits for the arbiter's answer before it is taken as queued. smile, smile_hold_s: the face's expression (source expression, through the head server) at the first clear face (track_min_face_px or more) of a conversation, once; smile_unseen: smile also when nobody is found.
